title: 1942 HHS Cadets. Rifle shooting practiced in the basement boiler room
description: Like the female cadets, the male cadets at Hartland High School met every Friday afternoon to train for World War II. They were issued painted wooden guns for practice—crude replicas with brown butts, silver triggers and barrels, and sometimes nails for triggers or a four-inch strip of tin as the trigger guard. Training began with exercises in the basement, followed by outdoor marching in rows to a steady beat. In this picture, the senior cadets are recognizable by their striped pants; some also trained with real guns, though never during school hours. Theoretical instruction was provided using large painted or printed boards and pictures stored in the furnace room. (Details by Harold Plummer)
